title: Supported complexes on an elementary etale neighbourhood: shriek and direct image
statement:
Work in the universes of [def-weil-size-convention]. Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme] and let $X,V$ be algebraic spaces over $S$ with their small etale structure sheaves [def-trf-algebraic-space]. Use module sheaves [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category] and unbounded derived categories [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Let $i:U\hookrightarrow X$ be an open subspace [def-a1-space-open-subspace] and $p:V\to X$ representable etale. Let $Z$ be the reduced closed subspace of $X$ with underlying set $|X|\setminus|U|$ [lem-sfb-space-reduced-closed-support], and suppose $V\times_XZ\to Z$ is an isomorphism. Put $T=U\times_XV$. Use exact etale restriction $p^*$ and its exact module extension-by-zero left adjoint $p_!$ [lem-sfb-space-elementary-shriek-exact], also denoting its termwise derived functor by $p_!$, and the canonical derived direct image $Rp_*$ [lem-sfb-space-derived-etale-chart-calculus]. For every $F\in D(\mathcal O_V)$ with $F|_T=0$, there is a canonical isomorphism $c_F:p_!F\xrightarrow{\sim}Rp_*F$. It is the morphism whose transpose under $p^*\dashv Rp_*$ is the inverse of the unit $F\to p^*p_!F$, which is itself an isomorphism. The counit $p^*Rp_*F\to F$ is an isomorphism, and $i^*Rp_*F=0$. In particular for every $M\in D(\mathcal O_X)$ and every integer $n$, the comparison $c_F$ and the adjunction $p_!\dashv p^*$ induce a natural bijection
$$\operatorname{Hom}_{D(\mathcal O_X)}(Rp_*F,M[n])\cong\operatorname{Hom}_{D(\mathcal O_V)}(F,p^*M[n]).$$
No quasi-compactness, perfectness, quasi-coherence, or boundedness assumption is imposed.

proof.text: Write $P=p^*$, $L=p_!$, and $R=Rp_*$. By [lem-sfb-space-elementary-shriek-exact], $L$ and $P$ are exact additive functors on module sheaves with their specified adjunction. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-derived-factorization] to obtain their termwise functors on unbounded derived categories, with the canonical shift comparisons. Use the localized degreewise adjunction of [def-weil-exact-derived-adjunction], whose unit and counit are the original ones applied termwise. Thus $L\dashv P$ on these derived categories. Also $P\dashv R$ by [lem-sfb-space-derived-etale-chart-calculus], since etale pullback is exact restriction. Denote the left adjunction's unit by $\alpha:\mathrm{id}\to PL$, and the right adjunction's unit and counit by $\eta:\mathrm{id}\to RP$ and $\varepsilon:PR\to\mathrm{id}$.

We will check cohomology sheaves on geometric stalks. The forgetful functor from module sheaves to abelian sheaves preserves kernels and cokernels by [lem-weil-pbc-module-sheaves-colimits-forgetful]. The geometric stalk functors preserve finite limits and all small colimits and detect isomorphisms by [lem-sfb-space-etale-conservative-geometric-points]. Therefore their induced module stalks preserve kernels (finite limits) and cokernels (quotients, computed as coequalizers), hence images and cohomology. A complex is zero, or a morphism is an isomorphism in its derived category, precisely when its cohomology sheaves are zero, or the induced cohomology maps are isomorphisms. Thus these tests may be made on every geometric stalk. Exact $L$ and $P$ similarly commute with cohomology: applying an exact functor to $\ker d/\operatorname{im}d$ gives $\ker F(d)/\operatorname{im}F(d)$.

Put $E=LF$. For a geometric point $\bar x$ of $U$, every lift $\bar v$ to $V$ lies in $T$. Since $F|_T=0$, the stalks $H^q(F)_{\bar v}$ are zero for every $q$. The stalk formula of [lem-sfb-space-etale-sum-stalks] and exactness give $H^q(E)_{\bar x}=\bigoplus_{p\bar v=\bar x}H^q(F)_{\bar v}=0$. Hence $E|_U=0$ by step 2 (restriction has these stalks by [lem-sfb-space-geometric-points-conservative], with the etale stalk-ring identifications in the sum-stalk lemma). For a geometric point $\bar x$ outside $U$, [lem-sfb-space-reduced-closed-support] says $Z\times_X\operatorname{Spec}\Omega$ is a closed subscheme with nonempty support. Its ideal in the field $\Omega$ is proper, hence zero. Thus $\bar x$ factors through $Z$. The hypothesis $V\times_XZ\cong Z$ then says that there is exactly one lift $\bar v$ of $\bar x$ to $V$. This argument uses the actual base-changed closed subscheme, without asserting that an arbitrary base change of $Z$ is reduced.

source.place: Tag 08GG(2), support assertion; stalk formula preceding Tag 08GV and sites-modules.tex Tag 0710 (lemma-stalk-j-shriek)

proof.text: The unit $G\to PLG$ on module sheaves sends a section $s$ over $(W\xrightarrow{a}V)$ to the sheafification of $s$ in the $a$-summand of the extension presheaf [def-weil-extension-by-zero-presheaf, lem-pur-site-restriction-module-adjunction-exact]. Indeed evaluation of a map out of that sum on its $a$-summand is its adjoint at $(W,a)$; for the identity of $LG$ this is exactly the displayed inclusion. On a geometric stalk at $\bar v$, the explicit germ formula of [lem-sfb-space-etale-sum-stalks] identifies this unit with the inclusion into the $\bar v$-summand of $\bigoplus_{p\bar w=p\bar v}G_{\bar w}$. Apply this degreewise to a representative of $F$, using the localized-unit normalization in step 1 and the cohomology calculation in step 2. If $p\bar v$ lies outside $U$, step 3 makes the sum a singleton and the unit is the identity. If $p\bar v$ lies in $U$, every summand and the source are zero since all lifts lie in $T$. Thus $\alpha_F:F\to PE$ induces an isomorphism on every cohomology stalk and is an isomorphism. No stalks outside these two cases exist.

Let $q:T\to U$ and $t:T\to V$ be the projections. The canonical etale base-change isomorphism in [lem-sfb-space-derived-etale-chart-calculus], applied to $p$ and $i$, gives $i^*RF\cong Rq_*t^*F=Rq_*0=0$. The last equality holds because an additive functor sends a zero object to a zero object. This is the required vanishing for the canonical derived direct image, with no boundedness or quasi-compactness assumption.

For any $B\in D(\mathcal O_X)$ with $B|_U=0$ and any $A\in D(\mathcal O_X)$, apply [lem-sfb-space-derived-hom-mayer-vietoris] to $(A,B)$ at degree zero. Its $U$ term and its two adjacent overlap terms vanish: $B|_U=0$ implies $B|_T=0$, so these are Hom groups into zero objects, including the shifted overlap term. Exactness therefore says that the actual restriction map $\operatorname{Hom}(A,B)\to\operatorname{Hom}(PA,PB)$ is bijective. Under $P\dashv R$, this is postcomposition with $\eta_B:B\to RPB$: the transpose of $\eta_B f$ is $\varepsilon_{PB}P(\eta_B)P(f)=P(f)$ by the triangle identity. Consequently $\operatorname{Hom}(A,\eta_B)$ is bijective for every $A$. To see invertibility explicitly, take $A=RPB$ to get $r:RPB\to B$ with $\eta_Br=1$. Injectivity for $A=B$ and $\eta_B(r\eta_B)=\eta_B$ give $r\eta_B=1$. Thus $\eta_B$ is an isomorphism. In particular, step 3 permits $B=E$.

source.place: Tag 08H9 (lemma-mayer-vietoris-hom), applied with supported second argument; Tag 08GG(1)(a)

proof.text:
Define $c_F=R(\alpha_F^{-1})\circ\eta_E:E\to RF$. Both factors are isomorphisms by steps 4 and 6. Its transpose under $P\dashv R$ is
$$\varepsilon_F\circ P(c_F)=\varepsilon_F\circ PR(\alpha_F^{-1})\circ P(\eta_E)=\alpha_F^{-1}\circ\varepsilon_{PE}\circ P(\eta_E)=\alpha_F^{-1}.$$
The middle equality is naturality of $\varepsilon$, and the last is its triangle identity. Hence this is precisely the comparison specified in the statement, not just an unspecified isomorphism between the same objects. The displayed equality also gives $\varepsilon_F=\alpha_F^{-1}\circ(P(c_F))^{-1}$, so the canonical counit $PRF\to F$ is an isomorphism. Units, counits, functor application and the inverse of a natural isomorphism are natural, so $c_F$ is natural on the full subcategory $F|_T=0$.

For $M\in D(\mathcal O_X)$ and $n\in\mathbf Z$, precompose with $c_F$ and apply $L\dashv P$ to obtain
$$\operatorname{Hom}(RF,M[n])\xrightarrow{h\mapsto h c_F}\operatorname{Hom}(LF,M[n])\xrightarrow{g\mapsto P(g)\alpha_F}\operatorname{Hom}(F,P(M[n])).$$
Both arrows are bijections. The canonical exact-functor shift comparison of [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-derived-factorization] identifies $P(M[n])$ with $(PM)[n]$. Thus the result is exactly the claimed natural bijection, for every integer $n$. Naturality follows from the two displayed formulas and from naturality of the shift comparison.

lean.statement: theorem supported_etale_excision {U T : AlgebraicSpace S} [HasDerivedCategory.{w} U.SmallModules] [HasDerivedCategory.{w} T.SmallModules] (i : U ⟶ X) (p : V ⟶ X) (hi : IsRepresentableWith (fun _ _ f ↦ IsOpenImmersion f.left) i.hom.hom) (hp : IsEtale p.hom.hom) (Z : ClosedSubspace X) (hZ : IsReduced (Z.val : AlgebraicSpace S)) (hSupport : pointImage Z.val.arrow.hom.hom = (pointImage i.hom.hom)ᶜ) (hIso : IsIso (Limits.pullback.snd p.hom Z.val.arrow.hom)) (q : T ⟶ U) (t : T ⟶ V) (sq : IsPullback q t i p) : ∃ c : (ObjectProperty.ι (fun F : V.DerivedModules ↦ IsZero ((spaceDerivedPullback t).obj F))) ⋙ spaceEtaleDerivedShriek p hp ≅ (ObjectProperty.ι (fun F : V.DerivedModules ↦ IsZero ((spaceDerivedPullback t).obj F))) ⋙ derivedDirectImage p, ∀ F : ObjectProperty.FullSubcategory (fun F : V.DerivedModules ↦ IsZero ((spaceDerivedPullback t).obj F)), IsIso ((spaceEtaleShriekAdjunction p hp).unit.app F.obj) ∧ (spaceEtaleShriekAdjunction p hp).unit.app F.obj ≫ ((spaceDerivedAdjunction p).homEquiv _ _).symm (c.hom.app F) = 𝟙 F.obj ∧ IsIso ((spaceDerivedAdjunction p).counit.app F.obj) ∧ IsZero ((spaceDerivedPullback i).obj ((derivedDirectImage p).obj F.obj)) ∧ ∀ (M : X.DerivedModules) (n : ℤ), Function.Bijective (fun h : (derivedDirectImage p).obj F.obj ⟶ M⟦n⟧ ↦ (spaceEtaleShriekAdjunction p hp).homEquiv F.obj (M⟦n⟧) (c.hom.app F ≫ h) ≫ (spaceEtalePullbackShift p hp n).hom.app M)
